# Module `lune_ui_core::widgets::virtual_list`

[API reference](../../INDEX.md) / parent [`lune_ui_core::widgets`](../widgets.md)

The virtualized list (`layout.virtualized-list`): only the rows in view are built, on a
[`scroll area`](scroll_area.md) that knows the whole extent. Selection is a set of
[`RowKey`](virtual_list.md#struct.RowKey)s, so a row keeps it when it scrolls away or the app replaces the data.

Rows are placed with an `f64` subtraction and a cast of the small result (D6): `top(i)` and the
offset can be tens of millions of pixels, where an `f32` steps in whole pixels. That is why the
list sits on [`Ui::scroll_area_untranslated`](../ui.md#method.Ui.scroll_area_untranslated).

Heights ([`RowHeights`](virtual_list.md#struct.RowHeights)): fixed rows are arithmetic; measured rows are a Fenwick tree of height
differences over an estimate, so `top(i)` and the row at an offset are O(log n). A frame's work
depends on the viewport, not on the row count: the only pass over the rows is the tree's when
the estimate changes or rows are added (amortised O(1) a row).

Frame order: the keys move the cursor before anything draws, so the reveal request reaches the
area this frame. Inside the area, every built row registers its region and takes its input, and
only then do the rows draw: a click moves the selection of all rows in the same frame, and a
child widget's region lands above its row's. A height measured for the first time takes effect
on the next frame (one catch-up frame); a change above the first visible row shifts the offset
by as much, so that row stays where it is on screen. A row's height follows the row, not its
index: what each row measured is kept by its [`RowKey`](virtual_list.md#struct.RowKey), and before the rows are placed those
in the window take the height they were measured at, so a sort or a replaced list places them
as a settled frame does and asks for no catch-up for rows already seen. A row never measured
stays on the estimate.

Source: `crates/lune-ui-core/src/widgets/virtual_list.rs:1`

<a id="struct.RowHeights"></a>
### Struct `RowHeights`

```rust
pub struct RowHeights {
    // some fields omitted
}
```

The rows' geometry: fixed arithmetic, or measured heights over an estimate. Positions are `f64`.

Measured rows keep each row's height (`own`, 0 until measured) and a Fenwick tree (`tree`, node
`i` sums the height differences from the estimate of the rows `(i - lowbit(i), i]`), so
[`Self::top`](virtual_list.md#method.RowHeights.top), [`Self::row_at`](virtual_list.md#method.RowHeights.row_at) and [`Self::set`](virtual_list.md#method.RowHeights.set) are O(log n). Rows `0..m` only touch nodes up
to `m`, which is why dropping rows is a truncation and adding them only computes the new nodes.

Source: `crates/lune-ui-core/src/widgets/virtual_list.rs:285`

**Methods and associated items**

`impl RowHeights`

- <a id="method.RowHeights.count"></a>`pub fn count(&self) -> usize`

  The number of rows.

- <a id="method.RowHeights.height"></a>`pub fn height(&self, i: usize) -> f64`

  Row `i`'s height.

- <a id="method.RowHeights.row_at"></a>`pub fn row_at(&self, y: f64) -> usize`

  The row holding `y`: the last row with `top <= y`, in `0..count` (0 for no rows or a `y`
  above the first).

- <a id="method.RowHeights.set"></a>`pub fn set(&mut self, i: usize, h: f32) -> f64`

  Records what row `i` measured and returns the change in its height: 0 for fixed rows, a
  row out of range or a height that is not finite.

- <a id="method.RowHeights.splice"></a>`pub fn splice(&mut self, at: usize, removed: usize, added: usize)`

  Rows `at..at + removed` give way to `added` rows not measured yet, and the rows after them
  keep their heights: an edit of a document that inserts or deletes lines, so a measured
  height follows its line. The tree is rebuilt from `at`, O(rows from `at`), on such an edit
  only: nothing calls it per frame. A range past the end is cut at the end.

- <a id="method.RowHeights.sync"></a>`pub fn sync(&mut self, count: usize, heights: Heights)`

  Brings the geometry up to this frame's `count` and `heights`. Free when neither changed.

- <a id="method.RowHeights.top"></a>`pub fn top(&self, i: usize) -> f64`

  Where row `i` starts; `top(count)` is the end of the last row.

- <a id="method.RowHeights.total"></a>`pub fn total(&self) -> f64`

  The height of all rows.

- <a id="method.RowHeights.window"></a>`pub fn window(&self, offset: f64, viewport: f64) -> std::ops::Range<usize>`

  The rows to build for a viewport of `viewport` at `offset`: those in view and [`MARGIN`](virtual_list.md#constant.MARGIN)
  above and below, one fewer below when the first row is cut, so uniform rows of height `h`
  never build more than `ceil(viewport / h) + 2 * MARGIN`.
